sentences.text:
The Food Inspector vs Jalla Narayana on 26 June, 2023
 The Honourable Sri Justice K.Surender
 Criminal Appeal No.469 Of 2023
Judgment:
1. The State represented by the Food Inspector is aggrieved by the acquittal recorded by the learned
Magistrate in C.C.No.363 of 2002 dated 06.03.2007.
2. Briefly, the case of the prosecution is that
on 01.04.2003, samples of ground nut oil was taken from the Hotel of the respondent/accused.
The same was sent for the purpose of analysis.
The analysis report was received on 06.04.2000.
Further, the complaint was filed on 13.10.2002.
No notice was sent after receipt of analysis report.
Analysis report was served on the accused subsequent to his appearance on 18.11.2002.
The Court found delay of nearly 3 years for the accused in coming to know about the analysis.

3. I do not find any infirmity with the order of the learned Magistrate when it is mandatory to sent a notice to the accused and the same was not sent under Section 13 (2) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act.
4. Accordingly, there are no grounds to interfere with the order of the learned Magistrate and Criminal Appeal is dismissed.
Miscellaneous applications pending, if any, shall stand closed.

_ K.SURENDER, J Date: 26.06.2023 dv The Food Inspector vs Jalla Narayana on 26 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/136315719/
